 Police Blotter: Inmate smuggled drugs into RI federal prison 
 Randy Diaz-Pizarro received an additional two years on his sentence

 By Colleen Cronin | ccronin@bostonherald.com PUBLISHED: November 9, 2026 at 8:10 PM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... An inmate is receiving additional time behind bars for smuggling drugs into the Rhode Island facility where he’s serving out his sentence .
 Randy Diaz-Pizarro, 34, was sentenced to an additional 24 months in prison, according to a statement from the Rhode Island U.S. Attorney’s Office, on top of the six years he received for a conviction in the District of Massachusetts.
 Diaz-Pizarro smuggled synthetic cannabinoids soaked into pieces of papers into the Wyatt Detention Facility in Central Falls, RI, working with several co-conspirators, including another inmate, a worker at the facility, and a person outside the prison, the statement said. “Diaz-Pizarro directed and coordinated payments and communications related to the scheme,” the office said.
 The court considered the Diaz-Pizarro’s criminal history and that he committed the offense while in custody for unrelated charges.
 “Randy Diaz-Pizarro is an unrepentant career criminal who smuggled drug-soaked papers into a detention center not only for his own use, but for his fellow inmates to purchase,” Special Agent in Charge of FBI Boston Ted E. Docks said in a statement. “His blatant disregard of the law undermined the safety of this facility.”
 “This sentence should serve as a warning: the FBI and our partners are working every day to identify and bring to justice those who seek to profit from criminal activity while behind bars,” he added.
 According to the Massachusetts U.S. Attorney , Diaz-Pizarro was already nabbed for his involvement with Boston’s Heath Street Gang on gun and drug charges. He pleaded guilty to those charges last years, court records showed. In addition to the prison sentence for those crimes, he received three years of supervised release set to start after his time behind bars.
 Incident Summary
 BPD responded to 206 incidents in the 24-hour period ending at 10 a.m. Monday, according to the department’s incident log . Those included one robbery, five aggravated assaults, three larcenies from a vehicle, 20 miscellaneous larcenies, and three auto thefts.
 Arrests
 All of the below-named defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty.
 — Helen Medina, 201 Heath St., Jamaica Plain. Assault and battery.
 — Benjamin Smestad, 38 Broad St., Quincy. Shoplifting by concealing merchandise.
 — Reginald Valcin, 19 Winthrop St., Malden. Operating under the influence of liquor.
 — Cheyenne McCall, no address listed. Assault and battery.
 — Deborah Baez, 433 Dudley St., Roxbury. Assault and battery with a dangerous weapon.
 — Amari Robinson, 433 Dudley St., Roxbury. Assault and battery.
 — Lauren Keating, 199 H St., Boston. Vandalizing property.
